## Cross-lens split on the same channel — and why Alternatives wins it

Methodology and Alternatives BOTH examined the tier-2 clearance channel and reached
different severities. Methodology: "a recipe-compliant suffixed-round PASS carries
`pod=<name>` and is skipped in both directions, so the channel is legacy/non-compliant
notes only" => bounded residual, APPROVE. Alternatives: reachable with NO relaunch from
documented standard shapes => Must-Fix, REVISE.

Alternatives wins on the MEASUREMENT. The Phase 1.5 fact-check measured #2223's real 7B
upload-verification PASS as carrying ZERO `pod=` tokens under the full `_note_pod_tokens`
grammar. So the "legacy/non-compliant" shape Methodology treats as the exception is the
CURRENT MAJORITY shape on live tasks. A residual bounded by "only non-compliant notes"
is not bounded when non-compliant notes are the norm.

The no-relaunch sequence (all four steps documented shapes): primary `epm:run-launched`
(MID-RUN, never verified) -> sibling `epm:run-launched` (structured-named) -> sibling's
round posts a PASS with `outroot=`/`rows=` but NO pod binding, keeping its pod for a
named next round so it stays LIVE -> operator runs `--primary-only --yes` believing the
primary done (the #825 false-DONE class the tag exists to backstop). Arm (i) satisfied;
the window anchors at the primary's ONLY launch so the sibling's pod-less PASS postdates
it and is in-window; tier-2 binds it; arm (ii) satisfied => CLEARED. A mid-run primary is
destroyed with the tag set and no `--force-keep-running`. §12.5(b)'s inverse trace missed
this because the window re-anchor only protects against PASSes PREDATING the newest

## Decision: adopt the pre-registered TIER-1 fallback for clearance arm (ii)

`Decision: arm (ii) requires a POD-BOUND upload-verification PASS naming the primary in
structured position (#1961 grammar). A tier-2 pod-less PASS NO LONGER satisfies the
keep-running clearance.` Reasons by weight:

1. **The plan's own kill criterion is armed** — it pre-registered exactly this fallback
   for exactly this trigger. Honoring it executes the recorded plan, not a new design.
2. **The asymmetry is decisive.** The clearance's entire marginal value is converting a
   loud-warning `--force-keep-running` override into a silent NOTE-and-proceed. A false
   positive destroys a running job. Removing a warning is not worth a shield bypass.
3. **The clarifier's binding wording requires it** — `epm:clarify v1` said per-pod
   evidence must clear the primary SPECIFICALLY, and a pod-less PASS is by construction
   not pod-specific.
4. **The motivating incident needs neither tier-2 nor the clearance.** #2223 carried
   `tags: []` — the tag was NEVER SET. The filed gap was purely that `--name-suffix`
   cannot name the primary and the bare form destroys both. The strict form costs the
   motivating case NOTHING; the primary-only SELECTOR (the deliverable) is untouched.
5. **It matches the ecosystem's direction** — CLAUDE.md's #1961 block calls the `pod=`
   token load-bearing, not stylistic. Requiring it for a DESTRUCTIVE clearance creates
   the right incentive.

Stated consequence: on today's note shapes the clearance will RARELY fire, so
`--primary-only` under a set tag will usually REFUSE and the operator uses
`--force-keep-running` (loud warning, recorded reason). That is the correct UX for "the
tag is for the sibling, destroy the primary anyway" — the warning is the feature.

NOT adopted (scope discipline): dropping the clearance entirely would contradict the

## Decision 1 — D6 validates against the READ-side slug grammar, not the write-side regex

`Decision: the terminate-side --name-suffix validation matches _POD_NAME_RE's slug
production (^[a-z][a-z0-9-]*$), NOT RUNPOD_NAME_SUFFIX_RE.`

This is strictly better than both alternatives on the table. It still closes the actual
hazard (the empty string fails a `^[a-z]...` anchor, so the shield-waived issue-wide
sweep is refused loudly), it keeps a real grammar check instead of narrowing to a
bare empty-string special case, and it has ZERO compatibility break because it
validates against exactly the grammar that decides which managed pod names can EXIST.
A non-empty suffix that no managed name could carry is a caller bug and now gets a
loud refusal instead of today's silent no-match fallthrough into stale-record cleanup
— strictly better error behavior, destroying nothing either way. `RunPodBackend.teardown`
recovers its slug from an existing `pod-<N>-<slug>` name that already matched
`_POD_NAME_RE`, so every argv it composes passes by construction, long slugs included.

## Decision 2 — duplicate names: termination semantics UNCHANGED, the new clearance fails closed

`Decision: --primary-only terminates EVERY live pod named exactly pod-<N> and no
suffixed sibling; the keep-running clearance FAILS CLOSED when the primary name
resolves to more than one live pod_id.`

Codex-methodology's remedy — refuse `--primary-only` outright unless exactly one live
exact-name match exists — is REJECTED as a regression. The bare path destroys every
same-name live pod deliberately: that is the #475 fix, where a stale local `pod_id`
terminated a ghost while a real RUNNING `pod-475` and an EXITED orphan survived and
kept accruing volume charges. A refusal-on-duplicates `--primary-only` would forfeit
exactly that orphan reaping on the path operators are being told to prefer.

The real defect is AC1's WORDING, not the design, so AC1 is restated as "every live
pod whose name is exactly `pod-<N>`, and no suffixed sibling" and gets a
duplicate-canonical test (RUNNING + EXITED both named `pod-<N>`, plus a live
`pod-<N>-b`: assert both primary ids terminate and the sibling survives).

Ambiguity matters only where the SHIELD IS BEING BYPASSED: a PASS naming `pod-<N>`
cannot say WHICH incarnation it attests, so with multiple live incarnations the
clearance cannot establish the primary is done and must not proceed silently. That
single fail-closed rule answers Codex-methodology MF2 and Codex-alternatives' C4
replacement-incarnation walk at once, without touching termination semantics. When the
tag is not set no clearance is needed and #475 reaping is unaffected.
